links.outcome: Fabrication (hallucination) of treatment options in ChatGPT-4 responses to foot and ankle cases
links.effect: ChatGPT did not fabricate treatment options; the no-fabrication criterion received the second-highest overall average score. Overall average case score was 22.7 of 25.
links.quote: Importantly, ChatGPT did not fabricate treatment options (ie, hallucination phenomenon), which has been previously well-documented in the literature, notably receiving its second-highest overall average score in this criterion.

links.outcome: Completeness of ChatGPT-4 clinical knowledge and treatment options for foot and ankle bone pathologies
links.effect: Average score 4.53/5 per criterion and 22.7/25 per case; lowest for hallux rigidus (21.3). Comprehensive information beyond standard treatment options was limited.
links.quote: ChatGPT struggled to provide comprehensive information beyond standard treatment options.

screen.reason: Evaluates ChatGPT-4's diagnostic and management accuracy across 8 orthopaedic clinical vignettes scored by fellowship-trained surgeons without evaluating a specific deployment practice or safeguard.
